findings.title: Office chairs at every desk pod face away from their desks, so seated coworkers sit facing into the backrest; 2 boardroom coworkers also sit backwards
findings.problem: Every pod chair is spawned rotated 180° wrong. The chair model's backrest is at local -z (`prefabs.ts:71`, back at z -.26, reclined with rotation.x -.12), so it faces +z. `meeting.ts:15` gives the chair `rotation: dz<0?Math.PI:0`. For the -z desk (dz=-.48) the chair sits at z-1 and is turned PI, so its backrest points +z, toward the desk. The same happens for the +z desk. The result is that all 32 empty chairs face away from their monitors (crop meeting-models-69: the seat faces the camera and the backrest touches the desk edge). Seated coworkers are oriented by `game.ts:133` (restYaw = atan2 toward the nearest desk), so they face the desk while the chair faces away. That pushes each blob's belly and arm stubs through the backrest. You can see it at the default game camera, not just close up: in meeting-models-01-start the purple and blue blobs at the bottom have orange or blue panels painted across their bellies, and meeting-models-68 is a zoom crop of a green blob with a blue backrest through its torso and an arm poking out of it. The boardroom has the opposite bug. Its chairs are rotated correctly (meeting.ts:30), but restYaw points every boardroom blob at the nearest pod desk (x≈4.85, to the west). The two blobs at x 10.8, (10.8,-7.9) and (10.8,-6.85), therefore face away from the table and into their chair backs (meeting-models-60, -55). There are about 22 coworkers in this room, and they are its main life and comedy. A whole office sitting backwards inside its furniture is the most visible modelling error in the level. It also breaks DR-70 (nothing interpenetrates at rest), which the audit can't catch because NPCs are not props.
findings.fix: 1) In src/levels/meeting.ts:15, change the chair rotation to `rotation:dz<0?0:Math.PI`, so the backrest is on the far side from the desk. 2) In src/levels/meeting.ts:30, push the boardroom NPC spots with an explicit yaw toward the table: `npcs.push({x,z,yaw:i%2?-Math.PI/2:Math.PI/2})`. NpcSpot already has `yaw?` (src/levels/types.ts:7). 3) Make restYaw robust: in game.ts:133, when seated, take the yaw from the chair prop under the NPC (nearest `chair` prop's rotation + PI) instead of the nearest desk, so blob and chair always agree. 4) Optional: shrink the seated blob or lift it, since its capsule bottom (y≈.395) is about 12 cm below the seat top (≈.52) and its .33 radius passes through the armrests at x ±.27 (prefabs.ts:73). Raise body.position.y for seated blobs from .35 to .45, or narrow the armrests to ±.31.
findings.verify: Retake meeting-models-01-start, -47 and -55/-60 with mockups/review5/tools/meeting-models/a.mjs, f.mjs and g.mjs. No chair backrest should be visible across any coworker's front, and the boardroom blobs at x 10.8 should face the table. Add a unit check: for every seated NpcSpot, the nearest chair's forward vector (rotation→+z) points within 30° of the blob's restYaw.

The x=13.2 pair face roughly the right way. findings.fix_correction: Steps 1 and 2 are right: `rotation:dz<0?0:Math.PI`, and boardroom `yaw:i%2?-Math.PI/2:Math.PI/2`. Step 3 is wrong as written. The chair's forward (its seat-facing direction) is local +z, and a blob's yaw also maps +z to its facing direction, so a seated blob's yaw should EQUAL the chair's rotation.y, not rotation + PI. With the chairs fixed, adding PI would turn every blob backwards again. Use `restYaw = nearestChair.spec.rotation ?? 0`.

findings.title: Win payoff is broken: window frames, sill and blinds draw on top of the projector slide, and the boardroom chart poster is mounted on a window pane
findings.problem: Back-wall windows are placed every 3.2 m by `windowXs` (decor.ts:70): x = …8.1, 11.3, 14.5. The only skip is x < -11.5 (decor.ts:124), so two windows sit right where the boardroom's projector screen goes. The screen's ink backing is a 4.4 × 2.5 box at (12.2, 1.9, z -9.82±.04) and the screen plane is at z -9.77 (decor.ts:151, 155). The window units are in the wall's upper group at local z .16–.26 (dressing.ts:27-31): the sky plane is at world z -9.84, the frame bars are .08 deep reaching z -9.76, the blinds are at -9.81 and the sill is box(w+.4,.06,.22) centred at -9.74. The window at 11.3 (frame x 10.0–12.6) therefore lies completely inside the screen, and the one at 14.5 (13.3–15.7) overlaps it by 1.1 m. Frame bars, mullion, sill and blind slats stick 1–3 cm in front of the screen plane. When the projector lights up, the player's reward image (the bar-chart slide) is crossed by white mullions, a horizontal sill, the blind slats and a second window's frame (meeting-models-39-win, -40-win-later, crop -61). The 'graph' poster `wallArt(back,'graph',15.2,1.9,.18,0,.9)` (decor.ts:129) is centred on the 14.5 window's glass: a poster hung on a window (meeting-models-30, -28, -40). The deadline clock at x -3.1, radius .34 (decor.ts:126), also overlaps the right frame of the -1.5 window by about 2 cm (frame half-width 1.28 → -2.78 vs clock edge -2.76; meeting-models-47). These are the hero shot and the end-of-level camera, so the defect is in every screenshot a player takes of the win. It breaks DR-72 (signage mounted on a wall face), DR-77 (overlapping coplanar faces) and DR-11 (a juicy, clean win frame).
findings.fix: In decor.ts meeting(): skip windows that intersect the boardroom back wall. Change line 124 to `backWindows(game,back,x=>x< -11.5||(x>9.3&&x<16.5),.2)`, which leaves the boardroom with a windowless back wall behind the screen. If you want a window there, keep the one at 14.5 but move the screen to x 11.3 and shrink it to 3.4 m wide, `box(3.4,2.1,.08)` / `PlaneGeometry(3.2,1.9)`. Move the 'graph' poster to a clear wall face, for example x 15.9 (only if the 14.5 window is skipped), or onto the boardroom glass frame post at x 13.8. Pull the screen plane forward to z -9.70 and the backing to -9.74, so no window part can ever sit in front of it. Move the clock to x -3.1 with s=.85, radius .29, or to x 0.1, which sits exactly between the -1.5 and 1.7 frames: gap from -0.22 to 0.42, radius .3 fits.

findings.title: The strip's load gauge (the room's only electricity readout) floats in mid-air in the boardroom doorway, and its show/hide logic is dead after decor freezing
findings.problem: `meeting-strip.ts:52` mounts the load gauge at (t.x+.95, 1.55, t.z+.06) = (13.25, 1.55, -2.19), and the comment there says it is "on the wall above the strip". The boardroom front at z -2 is glass only from x 9.3–11 and 13.8–16.5, with door posts at x 11 and 13.8 (decor.ts:144-146). x 13.25 is therefore in the open doorway. The gauge is a bare ink board with a decal (kit.ts:108) hanging 1.55 m up in empty air, and at the game camera it lines up with a boardroom chair, so it reads as a TV on a chair back (meeting-models-28, -30, -37, crop -63). It is the teaching instrument for the room's only electricity beat (the load budget, DR-47), so it must read as a device mounted on the strip or the wall. A second problem: `render()` toggles `this.gaugeMount.visible=g.stripPlaced()` (meeting-strip.ts:85). The mount is a child of `game.decorRoot`, and `freeze(this.decorRoot)` runs right after the MeetingStrip is built (game.ts:103 then :105). freeze merges its meshes into per-material buckets and removes the emptied group (kit.ts:77-85). The visibility toggle now acts on a detached group, so the gauge shows from frame 1, before the strip is placed (meeting-models-28 was taken before step 1 was done). This breaks DR-72 (nothing floats; signs are mounted) and DR-63 (gauges have housings, not bare boards).
findings.fix: 1) Mount the gauge on something solid. Either put it on the door post at x 13.8 facing +z, at (13.8+.0, 1.45, -1.93) with ry=0 and s=.7, plus a bracket `rbox(.1,.3,.08)` joining it to the post. Or mount it on the strip itself as a small dial housing on a stalk: `rbox(.36,.26,.12,.05)` at the strip's inlet end. 2) Give it a housing: in Gauge.mount (kit.ts:108) wrap it in `rbox(.78*s,.54*s,.12,.06)` in INK with a hood lip `box(.8*s,.05,.16)`, and finish the back with a `#3a3d55` panel. 3) Build the gauge (and any other runtime-toggled meshes: the kettle and heater hotParts, see the separate finding) under `game.root` instead of `game.decorRoot`, so freeze() doesn't swallow them. Then gaugeMount.visible works and the gauge appears only once the strip is placed.
findings.verify: Retake meeting-models-28 with c.mjs (before the strip is placed): no gauge visible. Retake -37 with d.mjs: the gauge sits on the post or strip with its outline touching a solid face. Orbit 180° (g.orbit(700)) at zoom 9: the gauge back is a finished housing.
findings.verify_reason: meeting-strip.ts:52 mounts the gauge under game.decorRoot at (13.25,1.55,-2.19). That is in the open doorway between the posts at x 11 and 13.8 (decor.ts:144-146), with nothing behind it (meeting-models-28, -30, -63, where it overlaps a chair). freeze(decorRoot) runs at game.ts:105, after MeetingStrip is built at game.ts:103. freeze removes every mesh from its parent and deletes the emptied groups (kit.ts:83), so `gaugeMount.visible` (meeting-strip.ts:85) toggles a detached group. I reproduced this: in verify-04 the snapshot reports stripPlaced=false, yet the gauge is visible. The needle still moves, because the merged mesh keeps the same CanvasTexture material.

mockups/review5/shots/verify-meeting-models-06-beanbag-reticle.jpg (gauge visible from the lounge before the strip is placed)
src/render/kit.ts:108 (Gauge.mount: bare box(.7s,.46s,.06) plus decal, no housing)

findings.title: The power strip is not the visible hub: the cable, the projector lead and both appliance cords plug into the generic black 'socket' box that covers the strip
findings.problem: The concept taught here is a load budget: three loads (kettle 2.5 A, heater 2 A, projector 1 A) share one strip whose 5 A breaker trips (meeting-strip.ts:1-7). The world should show that topology: reel → strip, and strip → three plugs. In the model it doesn't. Every cable level gets a generic target socket, `new T.BoxGeometry(.48,.38,.3)` in #384454 at (t.x,.25,t.z) = (12.3,.25,-2.25), plus a cyan torus at y .15 (game.ts:87-88). In the meeting the strip snaps to (t.x,.08,t.z+.3) = (12.3,.08,-1.95) (game.ts:211). The strip is .26 deep, so it butts against the box and lies half under its shadow and the ring, and its four outlets are hidden (meeting-models-32, -35, -37). The reel cable visibly ends in the black box (-35, -36). The projector lead is a decor tube that ends at (12.3,.05,-2.4), inside the box (decor.ts:150). Both appliance cords are drawn to (t.x+.25,.08,t.z), also the box, not the strip (meeting-strip.ts:94). A player sees a cable go into a black crate, three cords go into the same crate, and an orange strip lying next to it doing nothing. When the breaker trips, the pulsing red reset cap appears on the side of the box at (t.x+.32,.22,t.z) (meeting-strip.ts:89), not on the strip's own red switch (prefabs.ts:138). That teaches "the box trips", not "the strip trips on the sum of its plugs". It breaks DR-26 (the mechanic is the concept: plugging into the strip), DR-47 (device state on the device) and DR-37 (invisible wiring should be drawn). The plain BoxGeometry also has no edge radius (DR-58).
findings.fix: In the meeting, hide the generic socket box and ring once the strip is placed, or never create them for this level: in game.ts:88 skip `socket` when level.id==='meeting' and keep only the ring as the drop marker until stripPlaced(). Then make the strip the endpoint of every connection. The rope plug end should seat at the strip's inlet (stripAt().x-.5, .1, stripAt().z). The projector lead in decor.ts:150 should end at outlet 1 (x -.3 on the strip: 12.0,.16,-1.95). The kettle and heater cords (meeting-strip.ts:94) should end at outlets 3 and 4, with b = strip position + (-.3+k*.19, .16, 0). Add a small plug head, `rbox(.1,.08,.12,.03)` INK, at each plugged outlet. When an appliance is unplugged, move that plug head to the floor beside the strip, so the player sees an empty outlet. Move resetCap to the strip's own switch position (strip x + w/2-.06, y .16).
findings.verify: Rerun d.mjs and e.mjs. In -35 and -41 the strip's four outlets are visible with three plug heads seated and the cable entering the strip's end. In -37 the pulsing reset is on the strip. In -38 one outlet is visibly empty. Then try it on someone new: shown -35 only, they should say "three things are plugged into the strip".
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:88 builds an unrounded BoxGeometry(.48,.38,.3) socket at (12.3,.25,-2.25) for every cable level. The strip snaps to (t.x,.08,t.z+.3) (game.ts:211), half under the box and ring. The projector lead ends at (12.3,.05,-2.4), inside the box (decor.ts:150). Both appliance cords end at (t.x+.25,.08,t.z), also the box (meeting-strip.ts:94). The reset cap is placed at t.x+.32 (meeting-strip.ts:89), where t is the strip position from stripAt(), so it sits off the strip's switch. meeting-models-35 shows the cable entering the black box, the cords running to the box, and the orange strip peeking out underneath. -37 shows the tripped state.

findings.title: The grab cue is built flat and then rotated upright, so the 'floor brackets' stand vertically as floating yellow L shapes with half of them buried in the floor
findings.problem: The grab cue is meant to be "four floor-level corner brackets around whatever E would take" (game.ts:96 comment). Each bracket is built as a horizontal slab, `BoxGeometry(w,.03,d)` placed at (x,0,z) in an x-z ring (game.ts:97). Then game.ts:99 also sets `this.reticle.rotation.x=-Math.PI/2`. R_x(-90°) maps (x,0,z) to (x,z,0), so the whole cue stands up as a vertical picture frame through the target at y .03 (game.ts:436). The two lower brackets go to y≈-.5 under the floor, and the two upper ones stand about 0.5 m up in mid-air, facing one world axis regardless of the camera. In the shots they show as stray yellow L sticks next to beanbags, plants and desks (meeting-models-23, -25, -47, -48, -21, and crops -62, -65). From most yaws they are edge-on and invisible. The cue is one of the few allowed world-UI elements (AGENTS 2), and the only way to tell which of 300 props E will take (DR-18), so it has to read. As built, it reads as a modelling glitch, or as part of the prop.
findings.fix: Delete `this.reticle.rotation.x=-Math.PI/2;` from game.ts:99 (the brackets are already horizontal). Keep `reticle.position.set(mark.x,.03,mark.z)`. Scale the bracket ring to the prop footprint: `reticle.scale.set(max(.6,size[0]+.2)/1.06, 1, max(.6,size[2]+.2)/1.06)` from prefabs[kind].size, so the corners hug the base of big props like the desk and sofa instead of hiding under them. Optionally give the brackets a thin INK under-stroke (a slightly larger black copy at y .02) so they read on the pale floors.
findings.verify: Retake meeting-models-23 and -47 with c.mjs and f.mjs. Four yellow L corners should lie flat on the floor around the beanbag or bin, with nothing standing vertically. Orbit 8 yaws (g.orbit ±175): the corners stay visible on the floor from every yaw.
findings.verify_reason: The brackets are built flat as BoxGeometry(w,.03,d) at (x,0,z) (game.ts:97). game.ts:99 then sets reticle.rotation.x=-PI/2, which maps (x,0,z) to (x,z,0), so the frame stands vertically through the target at y .03. The lower corners end up under the floor and the upper ones about 0.5 m up. I reproduced this: in verify-06 there are two upright yellow L's above the beanbag, and in verify-03 an upright L beside a bin. In verify-07, after a 250 px orbit, the cue disappears edge-on. meeting-models-65 and -35 (upright brackets around the socket box) show the same.

findings.title: The coupler uses the plug's model, sits teal-on-teal on the mail cart, and the cable plug is the same yellow as its reel, so the job parts that teach the order (plug → coupler → reel) are hard to tell apart
findings.problem: The prefab builder draws `case 'coupler': case 'plug':` with the same geometry: a cylinder along x and two gold prongs (prefabs.ts:101-102). The cable's own plug is `makeProp('coupler','#ffcc52')` (game.ts:86). So the job item that joins two cables is a second plug, identical in shape and differing only in colour (teal #56d2c6, prefabs.ts:15). In meeting-models-33 and crop -64, the teal coupler on the floor and the yellow plug in Pip's mitt are the same object. Nothing in its shape says "socket on one end, prongs on the other", which is exactly the hidden-order rule R4B asked the parts to communicate (DR-37: order constraints show in the shape of the parts). On the cart the coupler is teal on the cart's teal-blue tray (#5f8fa8, prefabs.ts:16): at the default zoom in -49 and -59 it can't be found without the prompt, and at zoom 9 (-18) it is lost under the reel. At spawn, the plug (#ffcc52) lies against the anchor reel's flange (#ffc94d) at (anchor+.7, .3, anchor+.7) and blends into it (crop -10, -08), so the first thing the player must grab doesn't stand out (DR-43).
findings.fix: Give the coupler its own model in prefabs.ts: a short chunky barrel `rbox(.36,.22,.22,.06)` in job yellow #ffc94d with ink bands (two `box(.02,.23,.23)` INK rings). One end carries a socket face (an `cyl(.1,.1,.02,'x')` disc in #fff6e6 with two `box(.02,.05,.012)` INK slots). The other end carries the two gold prongs. Then it reads as a female-to-male joiner, the same family as the strip's sockets. Keep 'plug' as it is, but make the plug body INK with a yellow band so it contrasts with the reel flanges, or move the plug's start to the floor in front of the reel at (anchor.x+.9, .12, anchor.z+.9) so it doesn't overlap the flange. Change the mail cart colour for this level to a neutral (#9aa3b2 METAL or #6b7385) so a yellow coupler pops (meeting.ts:27: `color:'#8c96a8'`).
findings.verify: Retake c.mjs -16 and -18, g.mjs -59 (default zoom) and the d.mjs -33 crop. In a greyscale conversion the coupler is the highest-contrast object on the cart, and a viewer shown only the coupler crop can say which end takes the plug.
findings.verify_reason: prefabs.ts:101-102 shares one case for 'coupler' and 'plug' (a barrel along x with two gold prongs). game.ts:86 builds the cable's plug as makeProp('coupler','#ffcc52'), so the two differ only in colour (teal #56d2c6 vs yellow). meeting-models-64 shows the identical shapes. The cart is #5f8fa8 (prefabs.ts:16). At default zoom (my verify-13, prompt 'Grab the coupler') I could not pick out the coupler on the cart. It does stay on the cart, resting on the lip at y .744 at x -3.6, the cart's very edge. The plug at spawn blends with the reel flange and Pip in -10. Mitigating factor: a coupler badge appears after a failed mate (meeting-strip.ts:54-57,87), but that only shows after the player has failed the order, which DR-37 says should be visible before.

findings.title: Job-yellow is used by 32 desk mugs, a beanbag, desk lamps and the lounge pendant, while the job items themselves are orange (strip) and teal (coupler)
findings.problem: DR-45 says job items share one visual language: yellow #ffc94d/#ffc629 with ink stripes, and no decorative clutter uses it. In the meeting this is reversed. The mug prefab default colour is #ffc94d (prefabs.ts:12), and meeting.ts:16 places one mug per desk without a colour: 32 job-yellow cylinders across the office (meeting-models-16, -18, -33, -47). notes.models: The Big Meeting is the most complete-looking room. The overall model language matches the concept anchor: chunky rounded desks with keyboards, mice, pen cups and cable tails, five-star task chairs on casters, a ten-variant desk dressing, monitors with live screen textures, pillars with base, rail and cap trims and posters, server racks with hot LEDs and cable spaghetti, a framed whiteboard with scribble, a mail cart with posts, a parcel shelf and a push bar, and two-tone walls with windows, blinds and a sill. Outlines are dark ink: the darkest 2% of edge pixels measured 41–47 luma on the box and plant crops, which passes DR-56. Floor luma at the game camera is 148–182 (DR-54 OK), and ?norim (meeting-models-44) is nearly identical to the default, so the rim light is restrained. Where it falls short is layout and assembly more than missing polygons. The worst is that every pod chair is rotated 180°, so the 20 seated coworkers sit inside their backrests, and two boardroom blobs face away from the table. The win image has window frames and blinds drawn across the projector slide, and a poster mounted on a window. The load gauge floats in the doorway. The grab cue stands vertically. A plant sits inside a collider-less decor stack. The start-state audit reports 51 shallow overlaps (monitor/paper ×32, cabinet/box ×18, cart/reel). Every prop rests 2.5 cm under the visible floor because the floor collider top is at -0.025. Several key fixtures are 2–3-part placeholders: the coffee machine, water cooler, printer, projector, kettle, ping-pong table and socket box. Repetition (a 14-box raft that reads as a pallet, 18 identical cabinet+box units) undercuts the hand-made Good Job density. Beanbags still read as blobs or buns (DR-52/F5 open).
notes.clarity: The palette and object families work against clarity. Job yellow (#ffc94d) is on 32 desk mugs, a beanbag, desk lamps and the lounge pendant, while the job items themselves are an orange strip and a teal coupler. The coupler is literally the plug model in another colour, and on the teal mail cart it disappears at the default zoom. At spawn the plug is the same yellow as the reel flange. In the boardroom, the electrical topology (reel → strip → projector, kettle, heater) is not visible: every lead ends in the generic black socket box that half-covers the strip, and the reset light appears on the box. The grab cue meant to answer "what will E take?" is broken (rotated upright). The deadline clock, blinds, server-closet glow and the no-signal to slide screen swap do read well without text.
notes.playability: From a models standpoint, the camera works in most of the room: the floor reads, pillars fade, and the survey shows all walls at 1440×900 (meeting-models-02). Things that interfere with play: the lounge pendant fully covers Pip's head at zoom 9 and isn't an occluder; steam puffs up to 1.5 m wide sit over the kettle and boardroom glass; sprint-walking through the desk aisles knocks chairs, monitors and the box raft about (expected physics comedy, but the 14-box raft doubles as an obstacle wall next to the printer). There were no console or page errors in 9 script runs. snapshot().drawCalls reported 1236 at the start with fullfx; that counter includes the outline and post passes, so it isn't directly comparable to the ~175 LR15 figure, but it is worth a lowfx re-measure against DR-24.
notes.teaching: The one electricity beat (a load budget on a strip) is modelled as a strip lying next to a black box that everything plugs into. So the physical picture of "three loads summed on one strip" is missing: no plug heads in the strip's outlets, no empty outlet after unplugging the kettle, and the reset on the wrong object. The gauge does move through the green, yellow and red zones (4.5 A → yellow, trip → red), but it floats in mid-air and shows from frame one, before the strip exists in the doorway. The kettle reads as a toilet roll, so "unplug the kettle" is hard to act on by sight. The coffee machine's 30 m reel isn't connected to the machine by any cord, so the sneaky route's meaning ("borrow the coffee machine's power") is carried only by the prompt text.
notes.fun: The comedy set dressing is strong: coworkers with personalities and accessories, a lounge with sofa, ping-pong and beanbags, the boardroom audience, and slapstick-ready loose props (14 cartons, 32 mugs, bins and chairs all scatter when Pip sprints through, meeting-models-52/-53). The payoff moment, the projector going from no-signal to a glowing chart with confetti, is the right idea, but the window mullions and blinds drawn across it, plus Pip missing from the win push-in (QA 10 still open), take the shine off. Making the coworkers sit the right way round on their chairs is also a cheap fix that makes the whole office read as alive rather than glitchy.
